title: Bram and the Alibi
premise: Vesper Ishikawa, the unassuming archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, has spent years quietly untangling deaths the police misfiled as accidents, keeping her gift hidden behind locked crypt doors. When a confession letter arrives postmarked the day after the funeral of her friend, verger Bram Oduya, she realizes the killer is taunting her specifically—someone who knows both the case files and her secret methods. As Vesper follows the letter's riddles toward the drowned crypt and the tide that took the evidence, she discovers the killer is the one person who protected her for years: her mentor, Dean Corliss Hale, who killed to bury an old crime Vesper's own research was about to unearth. In the end, Vesper must choose between loyalty to the man who made her and the truth he taught her to serve, trapping him in his own confession as the tide returns what it took.
about_author: U. M. Iversen is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing centuries of quiet scandals in English cathedral archives. They write mysteries about people who know too much and say too little.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She catalogs the cathedral crypt on the eve of Bram Oduya's funeral, establishing her invisible life among the records and her habit of noticing what others file away. Emotional beat: grief held at arm's length, discipline as armor.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, flashback woven through present. We learn how she quietly solved three 'accidental' deaths over five years without ever telling police, using archive patterns no investigator reads. Beat: pride shadowed by loneliness; invisibility as both shield and cage.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A day after Bram's funeral, a confession letter arrives claiming responsibility for his death—but postmarked before the body was found. Beat: cold shock; the game has found her.

chapters.title: Detective Wren
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Detective Inspector Wren, who half-suspects Vesper's uncanny past insights. He warns her off the case while quietly asking for help. Beat: wary alliance forming; two people who distrust each other need each other.

chapters.title: What Bram Kept
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Searching Bram's quarters, she finds his own notes on the three old deaths—he knew what she'd done, and had been investigating a fourth name. Beat: betrayal-tinged tenderness; her friend was protecting her.

chapters.title: The Tide Table
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The letter's first riddle points to tide tables and the flooded lower crypt, where evidence surfaces only at spring low tide. Beat: dread mixed with the thrill of pursuit; the killer knows her methods intimately.

chapters.title: Dean Hale's Kindness
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Flashbacks to Dean Corliss Hale mentoring her, contrasted with his oddly specific questions now about her archive work. Beat: unease beneath gratitude; the reader feels what Vesper refuses to.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At spring low tide, Wren retrieves a satchel from the crypt sump containing Bram's missing notebook—pages torn out. Beat: hope curdling; someone reached the evidence first.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Reconstructing the torn pages from ink impressions, she finds a fourth victim from decades ago—a young organist whose death made Hale's career possible. Beat: vertigo; the pattern is older than she imagined.

chapters.title: Confession, Second Letter
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. A second letter arrives quoting her private archival notes verbatim—notes only accessible to someone with keys and clearance. Beat: terror; the killer is inside her sanctuary.

chapters.title: Suspects Among the Faithful
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren works the shortlist: the sacristan, the bell-ringer captain, the fundraising chair—all with access and motive. Beat: procedural tension; every suspect fits, which means none do.

chapters.title: The Alibi
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She realizes the title of the letters' postmark trick: the killer built himself an alibi out of the funeral itself, standing beside her when the letter claims the murder happened. Beat: chilling clarity; only one person stood there.

chapters.title: Denial
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She tests her theory against Hale and finds it holds—and hates herself for testing it. Beat: grief and self-betrayal; loyalty fighting truth in real time.

chapters.title: Wren's Doubt
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren discovers Vesper's history of unofficial investigations and confronts her, threatening to charge her as an accessory if she withholds more. Beat: fracture; her invisibility weaponized against her.

chapters.title: The Organist's File
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. In the diocesan deep archive she finds the sealed file on the organist's death, signed closed by a young Corliss Hale. Beat: grim confirmation; the mentor's whole life is built on the buried crime.

chapters.title: Spring Tide Warning
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The final spring tide approaches—the last chance to recover the rest of the evidence before it's swept to sea. Both realize the killer will act. Beat: ticking clock; converging dread.

chapters.title: The Trap in the Reading Room
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. She plants a forged document suggesting the organist file still exists elsewhere, then lets Hale see her hide it. Beat: cold resolve; the student sets a trap using the teacher's own lessons.

chapters.title: Night Keys
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Watching the archive through the night, Wren sees Hale enter after hours and take the bait—confirming everything but catching nothing yet. Beat: coiled suspense; proof without arrest.

chapters.title: The Drowned Crypt
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Hale corners Vesper in the flooding lower crypt, confessing with terrible gentleness that he killed to protect the church—and her. Beat: climax; water rising, truth finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Up
chapters.summary: Climax continued, alternating POV. Wren arrives as the tide turns; Hale, choosing not to drown them both, surrenders as the water releases the organist's remains and the final page of Bram's notebook. Beat: catharsis; the sea returns what it took.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At the inquiry, Vesper testifies openly for the first time, ending her career of invisible solutions; Wren stands witness for her. Beat: bittersweet vindication; truth costs, and pays.

chapters.title: The Open Door
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, epilogue. Months later, she reopens the crypt to the public, cataloguing Bram's restored notebook under her own name instead of anonymity. Beat: quiet renewal; memory honored, invisibility set down like a key returned.
